member.name: T:UiPath.Robot.Activities.Api.IProfilingCollector
member.summary:
The profiling feature works by collecting execution details for each activity that is being run (such as the start and end timestamps, the activity id or whether the activity threw an exception) and outputting them into a file. This data can then be used for multiple purposes, such as analyzing performance or identifying bottlenecks.
This interface can be used to augment the basic data with additional information that may be relevant for profiling. The received data is written directly to the JSON output file, alongside the basic information, so it is important for it to be a valid JSON string.

member.name: P:UiPath.Robot.Activities.Api.IProfilingCollector.IsProfilingEnabled
member.summary: Whether profiling data is being collected in the current run. If false, all calls to are silently discarded.

member.name: P:UiPath.Robot.Activities.Api.IProfilingCollector.ProfilingLimitReached
member.summary: Whether the collected event count limit has been reached. If true, subsequent are silently discarded.

member.name: P:UiPath.Robot.Activities.Api.IProfilingCollector.Diagnostics
member.summary: Per-run diagnostic opt-ins that Studio/Helm injected via JobProfilingOptions.Diagnostics. Null when the caller did not request any. UIA reads to decide whether to enable runtime data collection for this run, without going through the legacy InternalArgumentsDictionary["dataCollectionOptions"] path.

member.name: M:UiPath.Robot.Activities.Api.IProfilingCollector.LogProfilingData(System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Appends data, formatted as JSON, to the profiling output of an activity.
member.param: The instance id of the calling activity.
A valid JSON string containing activity specific data.

member.name: E:UiPath.Robot.Activities.Api.IProfilingCollector.OnProfilingDataCollected
member.summary: Event to be raised when profiling data is received.

member.summary: Per-run diagnostic opt-ins populated by Studio/Helm when starting a run that wants non-default diagnostics behavior (e.g. profiling-time UIA data collection). Null on runs that don't request anything special.

member.name: T:UiPath.Robot.Activities.Api.Profiling.UiaDataCollectionOptions
member.summary: Per-run enable flags for the UIA package's runtime data collection pipeline. Read by UIA's ExecutorRuntimeExtensions.LoadUIAExecutionFlags via .

member.name: P:UiPath.Robot.Activities.Api.Profiling.UiaDataCollectionOptions.ScreenshotsPath
member.summary: Absolute path where UIA should save runtime screenshots when cloud upload is unavailable or disabled. Null = use the legacy global default (%LOCALAPPDATA%\UiPath\ProfiledRuns\Screenshots). Helm and Studio Desktop set this to a per-run subdirectory of the profiling output dir so each profiled run's screenshots live alongside its *.uistat files.

member.name: P:UiPath.Robot.Activities.Api.Profiling.UiaDataCollectionOptions.MaxScreenshots
member.summary: Upper bound on how many screenshots UIA keeps on disk for a single run. Acts as a rolling window: once the count reaches this value, the oldest screenshot is evicted before a new one is written. 0 means unlimited. Helm and Studio Desktop default to 100; callers (Autopilot, CI, custom integrations) can override per run to trade disk pressure against retained evidence.
